label: EDGE AI / RESEARCH
title: Edge AI benchmark validation
subtitle: Reliability of Edge AI · KU Leuven
description: Embedded benchmark execution, host-to-board comparisons and a reproducible baseline for studying hardware faults.
metricLabel: anomaly windows validated against the host
goal: Establish how hardware bit flips affect TinyML inference, then assess software techniques that improve resilience.
work: Implemented and validated keyword spotting, image classification, anomaly detection and visual wake words benchmarks on nRF52840 DK under Zephyr.
Built Python evaluation workflows and documented reproducible firmware builds and numerical comparisons.
results: 48,608 anomaly-detection windows across 248 recordings matched the aligned host outputs exactly.
The anomaly evaluation achieved a mean-machine ROC AUC of 0.858. Numerical agreement and model quality are separate measurements.
next: Establish and run fault-injection experiments to assess bit-flip reliability.
Apply software-implemented fault-tolerance techniques and compare protected and unprotected benchmarks.
Deliver a final technical report documenting methods, results and limitations.
architecture: The nRF52840 DK runs embedded inference under Zephyr with TensorFlow Lite Micro.
Python workflows compare board outputs with an aligned host reference, supporting numerical checks before reliability experiments.
interpretation: Exact agreement applies to the evaluated anomaly-detection windows; it does not establish immunity to hardware faults.
ROC AUC describes anomaly-detection quality. Fault-injection and protection experiments are the next research stage.

label: FIRMWARE / AUTOMOTIVE
title: EV dashboard and ADAS warnings
subtitle: EV Dashboard & ADAS · Emertxe
description: An EV dashboard and driver-assistance warning system built around sensor inputs, vehicle states and serial telemetry.
goal: Combine real-time EV parameter monitoring with proximity-based warning features in an embedded prototype.
work: Developed the dashboard and warning system using STM32F103C8T6 and PICSimLab.
Integrated ultrasonic sensing, collision and blind-spot warning features, vehicle state management and UART telemetry.
results: Completed the implementation during the June–July 2026 Emertxe online internship.
Delivered a prototype combining vehicle monitoring and warning logic.
architecture: Ultrasonic sensor inputs feed the STM32 warning logic for collision and blind-spot indications.
Vehicle state management coordinates EV monitoring, while UART provides a telemetry communication path.
PICSimLab supports simulation of the embedded dashboard and warning behavior.
interpretation: The deliverable combines sensing, vehicle states, dashboard monitoring and warning logic in an internship prototype.
The warning features demonstrate embedded integration; no road-testing or production ADAS certification is claimed.

label: IOT / CONNECTIVITY
title: LOCAT’IT GPS-independent tracking
subtitle: LOCAT’IT · Team academic project
description: A team prototype exploring GPS-independent asset tracking using LoRa communication and real-time signal-strength display.
metricLabel: LoRa signal-strength readings displayed on OLED
goal: Explore whether one portable receiver can guide a user towards a tagged asset using changes in LoRa signal strength, without GPS coordinates.
work: Contributed to hardware integration, report preparation and the team presentation.
Worked within a three-person project team, with software and PCB design contributions shared across the group.
results: The team established communication and displayed RSSI values on an OLED screen.
Reported RSSI readings stayed around −92 to −107 dBm and changed too little with proximity to support reliable direction finding.
The project did not achieve the complete tracking objective; signal reception and display formed the working baseline.
architecture: The report’s final-device description pairs an Arduino / SX1278 transmitter with an STM32 / SX1278 receiver and OLED display.
LoRa packets provide a wireless link; the receiver presents RSSI readings as feedback about signal strength.
The intended tracking method uses readings collected while moving the receiver. RSSI alone does not directly measure direction of arrival.
Proposed follow-up work included calibrated distance estimation, measurements from multiple receiver positions and alternative radio or antenna tests.
interpretation: The report discusses Raspberry Pi and ESP32-C3 configurations alongside its final Arduino / STM32 description. These reflect development iterations, not one combined hardware configuration.
Range figures in the report are estimates. No validated positioning accuracy or measured energy saving is claimed here.

label: ROBOTICS / CONTROL
title: Autonomous line-following robot
subtitle: Autonomous Line-Following Robot
description: Real-time PID control and sensor calibration for an autonomous line-following prototype.
goal: Improve line-following behavior through real-time control and calibrated sensor feedback.
work: Implemented PID trajectory control on ARM Cortex-M.
Optimized sensor calibration and processing timing.
results: Implemented real-time PID trajectory control and sensor calibration on ARM Cortex-M.
architecture: Sensor readings provide feedback about the robot’s position relative to the line.
The PID controller uses tracking error to adjust the robot’s trajectory in real time.
Sensor calibration and processing timing support the feedback loop on the ARM Cortex-M platform.
interpretation: Performance depends on the track, sensor calibration and controller tuning. No numerical accuracy or latency claim is made without a retained measurement method.

label: IOT / SENSOR SYSTEMS
title: Smart parking IoT system
subtitle: Smart Parking IoT System
description: An ultrasonic sensing prototype that publishes parking-slot availability to a live dashboard.
goal: Make parking availability visible through a connected sensor system.
work: Integrated ultrasonic sensors with an ESP / Wi-Fi platform.
Built live slot monitoring through a dashboard.
results: Integrated ultrasonic sensing and a Wi-Fi dashboard to show parking-slot availability.
architecture: Ultrasonic sensors detect whether monitored parking spaces are occupied.
The ESP / Wi-Fi platform communicates slot availability to the dashboard.
The dashboard presents live availability so a user can identify a free space before searching manually.
interpretation: The prototype demonstrates connected occupancy monitoring. No measured reduction in parking search time is claimed.
